# SwiftWorkflowBuilder

Generates GitHub Actions workflows that build and test a Swift package.

The main workflow contains concise jobs which call generated, repository-local reusable workflows for Swift Package Manager and Xcode builds.

(Not to be confused with `swift-ci`, the Swift project's own CI bot. This tool is unrelated to it; it just borrows the `swift ci` command.)

## Requirements

- Swift 6.2 toolchain (for building this package)
- macOS 26 or later

## Installation

The easiest way to install the tool is with Mint:

```shell
mint install elegantchaos/SwiftWorkflowBuilder
```

(If you need to install Mint first, the easiest way is probably with Homebrew: `brew install mint`)

This installs an executable called `swift-ci`. As long as Mint's bin folder (`~/.mint/bin`) is on your `PATH`, the `swift` command finds it, so you can run it as `swift ci`. If `swift ci` reports an unknown subcommand, `~/.mint/bin` is missing from your `PATH`.

## Usage

To generate workflows for the package in the current directory:

```shell
swift ci generate
```

You can also pass the path to a package:

```shell
swift ci generate <path-to-your-package>
```

To run the tool from a checkout of this repository without installing it:

```shell
swift run swift-ci generate <path-to-your-package>
```

The tool writes three files into `.github/workflows`:

- the configured caller workflow, such as `Tests.yml`
- `SwiftWorkflowBuilderSwiftJob.yml` for Swift Package Manager jobs on macOS and Linux
- `SwiftWorkflowBuilderXcodeJob.yml` for simulator-backed Xcode jobs

Xcode build jobs use a generic simulator destination without selecting or booting a device. Xcode test jobs select and boot an available simulator before running tests.

Test-target source imports are inspected when these files are generated. On supported Swift versions, the Swift helper emits XCTest and Swift Testing commands only for the frameworks the package actually uses; older compilers and unrecognized test infrastructure use one combined `swift test` command.

Packages whose workflows were generated by ActionBuilderTool can simply run `swift ci generate`: it writes the new job files, and replaces the old README header. Delete the old `ActionBuilderSwiftJob.yml` and `ActionBuilderXcodeJob.yml` files afterwards.

### Options

`swift ci generate` accepts a few options:

- `--create-config`: makes a new `.swift-ci.json` file in the package directory.
- `--edit-config`: opens the package's settings file for editing.
- `--reveal-config`: reveals the package's settings file in the Finder.

## Configuration

The exact steps that the workflow executes can be configured.

These include:

- platforms to test, from: macOS, iOS, tvOS, watchOS, linux
- swift versions to test against: 5.10, 6.0, 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.4 and the main snapshot.
- the configuration to test: debug, release
- whether to run tests or just build
- whether to upload build logs
- whether to post a notification to a slack channel
- whether to amend a header to the README
- whether to test against every requested swift version, or just the earliest and latest

These settings are read from a `.swift-ci.json` file in the root of the package directory. A package that only has an `.actionbuilder.json` file, the name used before the tool was renamed, keeps using it; rename it to `.swift-ci.json` at your convenience. If neither file exists, some defaults are chosen.

If they aren't explicitly set in the settings file, the code attempts to pick sensible values by examining the `Package.swift` manifest:

- the tool version of the manifest is used to determine the version of Swift to test against.
- the platform minimum deployment versions listed in the manifest are used to determine platforms to test against

If the package manifest includes a minimum deployment for `.custom("Ubuntu", ...)`, the `linux` platform is added. The version number specified in this minimum deployment is currently ignored, but may eventually be used to determine the version of the runner image to use for the `runs-on: ubuntu-` entry of the workflow job.

If no minimum deployment information is present, the `macOS` and `linux` platforms are added by default. If these defaults aren't what you need, you can specify exact values using a settings file (see below).

### Settings Format

In an ideal world I'd like all of the configuration information that the tool requires to be extracted from the `Package.swift` file.

However, there are some situations where you may want to customise the behaviour slightly.

In this case you can add a `.swift-ci.json` file at the root of the project.

Here is an example:

```json
{
    "name": "TestPackage",
    "owner": "TestOwner",
    "platforms": ["macOS", "linux"],
    "compilers": ["swift510", "swiftNightly"],
    "configurations": ["release"],
    "test": true,
    "header": false,
    "firstlast": false,
    "uploadLogs": false,
    "postSlackNotification": false
}
```

### History

This code was originally part of [Action Status](https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/action-status/id1498761533), which is a little macOS/iOS tool I made for monitoring GitHub Actions.

It was split out as ActionBuilderCore, with a command line tool called ActionBuilderTool and an [SPM command plugin](https://github.com/elegantchaos/ActionBuilderPlugin). Version 3 renamed the package to SwiftWorkflowBuilder and the tool to `swift-ci`, and dropped support for the plugin, which keeps working with 2.x releases.
